title: EU AI Act Article 30 — Notifying Authorities and Notified Bodies for AI Conformity Assessment
context: 2026-08-29 engine cycle — Article 30 governs the designation and oversight of notified bodies that perform third-party conformity assessment for high-risk AI systems, critical for the August 2026 enforcement horizon
body: EU AI Act Article 30 establishes the framework for notifying authorities (designated by Member States) and notified bodies (the independent third-party assessors) that conduct conformity assessments for high-risk AI systems under Annex III. A notified body must demonstrate impartiality, technical competence, and appropriate liability insurance. Notifying authorities must assess and monitor notified bodies against the requirements of Article 31-33, and the Commission maintains a publicly accessible database of all notified bodies (Article 30(7)). When a notified body conducts a conformity assessment, it must produce an EU-type examination certificate or quality system approval — documents that the provider uses to affix the CE marking and draw up the EU declaration of conformity. The Council of AI measurement infrastructure supports this by providing verified measurement credentials that a notified body can rely on rather than re-performing every measurement from scratch. Concretely: (1) a provider undergoing Article 43 conformity assessment can present Council-signed per-axis measurement evidence to the notified body; (2) the notified body validates the signatures offline and incorporates the verified measurements into its assessment report; (3) this reduces the cost and timeline of third-party assessment while maintaining the evidentiary chain required under Articles 11 and 43. The honest boundary is monitored containment: the notified body verifies that measurements exist and are independently signed — it does not claim the system is provably safe, only that the risk controls are measured and watched.
